name: Lake Lanier
type: Clear, deep highland lake; blueback herring

stripers.doing: Very good when the weather cooperates. Before a front, stripers are on the surface in the middle to back ends of creeks; after a front they go down. Keep moving until you see them on top or on the graph.
how: Lead-head fluke, bucktail or small jerkbait at rolling fish, or freelined herring and trout.
Downlined herring or trout, or a Captain Mack four-arm U-rig.
Gulls and loons over the water usually mean stripers are near.
Live or cut bait near the birds: one rod under a slip float at 15 ft, one on the bottom.

spots.doing: Follow ditches out of the creeks to the main river channel; bass gather in small areas around 40 ft.
how: Finesse worm or small lizard on 6 to 8 lb fluorocarbon, under the boat or worked down the channel.
Straight down when fish show on the graph.
McStick jerkbait, Fish Head Spin or deep crankbait, slowly.

crappie.doing: Tough but steady: deeper docks and brush in 17 ft or more. The depth that holds fish changes day to day.
how: Shoot a jig under docks and let it fall until it stops.
Twitch a Microspoon slowly over the brush.
Slow; cold fish need time to look at the bait.

stripers.doing: Stripers push up the rivers and creeks with the herring as the water warms through the 50s. The upper lake and river channels hold the most fish.
how: Herring or gizzard shad about 40 ft behind the boards.
Unweighted bait 60 to 120 ft back on slow days.
Creek backs on warm afternoons; points and clay banks are steadier.

spots.doing: In March, the top pros fished rocky mid-lake and lower-lake points, many off islands, from 5 to 30 ft, and skipped points with mushy bottoms.
how: Keitech or YUM Pulse on 1/4 oz, cast across points and crawled.
Ned rig or drop shot at 25 to 35 ft on the sides of long points near brush.
Jerkbait along riprap and marina walkways.
Finesse fishing on deep points was best on calm days.

crappie.doing: Crappie move from creek mouths toward the middle and backs of creeks onto stumps, laydowns, fish attractors and creek ledges.
how: Longline or spider-rig jigs and minnows through creek channels.
Minnow under a float on laydowns and brush.
Warm afternoons after a few warm days in a row.

stripers.doing: Most fish are up the rivers: the Chestatee channel from Vanns Tavern to Toto Creek and the Chattahoochee up to Clarks Bridge. Points and clay banks are the most consistent; creek backs hold the warmest water.
how: The most productive method. Herring or gizzard shad; shad in creek backs, herring in the river.
40 to 60 ft back, 120 ft or more on slow days; a heavy freeline with split shot.
On fish marked at 20 to 25 ft.

spots.doing: Largemouth bed in pockets in the 60s; spotted bass bed deeper, often 10 to 15 ft, on gravel and flat rock. The full moon pushes waves of fish up.
how: Shaky head, wacky rig or Fluke around beds and the bank between them.
Jerkbait across the points into spawning coves.

crappie.doing: Crappie spawn in the backs of creeks in a few feet of water once it reaches about 62 to 65°F.
how: Float and jig or minnow in 1 to 6 ft.
Double jig rig longlined across the flats.

stripers.doing: The herring spawn on points, clay banks, riprap and marina walls at first light, and stripers crash them. By June they slide to brush on points in 15 to 35 ft, then deeper.
how: Walking bait, popper or wake bait on points and humps.
Herring pitched or freelined to points.
Downlines over brush in 15 to 35 ft.

spots.doing: The herring spawn is the best shallow bite of the year: red clay points, bridge pilings, blow-throughs and marina walls at first light. Then long clay points and rocky flats in under 20 ft.
how: Topwater worked slowly around the spawn.
Spot Choker underspin, white spinnerbait or chartreuse Fluke run parallel to marina walls.
Topwater on humps and the ends of long points.

crappie.doing: Fish move off the banks back to docks, most in 10 to 15 ft or less, chasing bait. Big schools roam near the creek channel.
how: Pearl-white or purple soft jigs, or a blue-and-chartreuse hair jig.
Singles and small groups are the best chance at a trophy.

stripers.doing: Fish move south to deeper, cooler water with oxygen. Early August: main-lake pockets at 50 to 70 ft in the morning, then creek and river channels at 90 to 120 ft as the sun rises.
how: 2 oz sinker, 6 to 10 ft of 10 to 15 lb fluorocarbon, 1/0 octopus hook, live herring.
Ben Parker spoon or 1 to 2 oz white bucktail with a trailer, about 2.8 mph, 8 colors out.
Chrome Boss Hawg or Ben Parker spoon burned up through the school.
Keep bait water 50 to 65°F; use a Seaqualizer on fish when the surface is over 80°F.

spots.doing: Shallow in creek and pocket backs early, then 25 to 45 ft on sharp breaks, point ends and hump sides, moving to timber edges at 35 to 45 ft.
how: Spook Jr., swimbaits and a weighted Fluke; the topwater bite can die in extreme heat.
Flutter spoon, rip-pause-rip; strikes come on the fall.
Long leader of 6 to 8 lb fluorocarbon.

crappie.doing: Suspended 15 to 25 ft over a 30 to 40 ft bottom near deep brush, blowdowns off steep banks and shaded docks.
how: 1 to 1.5 inch jig on a 1/24 oz head; give it time to fall.
Set 15 to 20 ft deep over 20 to 25 ft.
Shaded docks; the biggest fish often bite first.

stripers.doing: Schools move from the south end up toward mid-lake and blow up at random times. Topwater is best early and late on sunny days and any time on cloudy days.
how: Magic Swimmer in wind, Drift Walker or Spook in calm water; come in upwind.
Nickel in sun, pearl in clouds; drop about 20 ft below marked fish and power-reel up.
Herring freelined about 100 ft back across humps and points.

spots.doing: Shallow ditches in creeks hold bait at daylight; follow them out to 25 to 50 ft. Points, humps, steep riprap and roadbeds near 40 ft also hold fish.
how: Shad Spin slow-rolled or a crankbait slow-cranked at daylight.
Long casts, jerk-jerk-pause, pauses up to 10 seconds.
Jigging spoon or drop shot with minimal movement.

crappie.doing: October: docks with brush or shade, fish 10 to 15 ft down over 30 to 40 ft. November: open-water brush 5 to 14 ft deep over 12 to 20 ft.
how: Cast into the shadows; bright jigs in clear water, dark after rain.
Minnows took about 60 percent of November fish.
Small hair jigs with little action.
